hook: Andrej Karpathy has spent his career moving between building frontier neural networks and teaching other people how they work. He was a founding research scientist at OpenAI in 2015, then spent five years as Tesla's Director of AI leading the computer vision team behind Autopilot and Full Self-Driving. Along the way he designed and taught CS231n, Stanford's first deep learning course, and built a large public following through blog posts and YouTube lectures that walk through how language models are actually built. After a second stint at OpenAI and a run at his own AI education venture, Eureka Labs, he joined Anthropic's pretraining team in May 2026.

standing.watch: What remains unresolved in the records is the outcome of the lawsuits tied to OpenAI and Anthropic, all of which are filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet. The most recent filings listed are Buist v. Anthropic, PBC on 2026-10-07 and Bass v. OpenAI, LLC on 2026-09-28, with others from September 2026. The records do not show any pending listing, funding event, or valuation for OpenAI, Tesla, or Eureka Labs. The single news story naming Karpathy, from 2026-10-03, points to a focus on directing AI agents, but the records do not state what that work will produce. His move to Anthropic's pretraining team in May 2026 is the latest position recorded, and no further development is noted.
standing.record: The site's records connect Karpathy to two companies, OpenAI and Tesla, and to a set of lawsuits that name OpenAI entities and Anthropic rather than him personally. Those cases include USA Today Co. v. OpenAI Foundation, TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, and JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, along with Buist v. Anthropic, PBC. Each is recorded as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. The pattern across the record is a career split between building models at OpenAI and Tesla and explaining them publicly, with the legal exposure sitting with the companies he has worked for. Coverage naming him is limited to one story, dated 2026-10-03, about a shift from coding to directing AI agents.
standing.standing: Andrej Karpathy stands in the records as a researcher who has moved between the largest AI labs and a public teaching role. He is listed as a co-founder of OpenAI, founded in 2015, and as an executive of Tesla, the public company based in Palo Alto. His profile places him at Anthropic's pretraining team from May 2026, after founding the AI education venture Eureka Labs in 2024. The records also note his return to OpenAI from 2023 to 2024, where he built a team focused on midtraining and synthetic data generation. His influence in the site's account rests on frontier model work and on CS231n, the Stanford deep learning course he designed and taught.

achievements.title: Founding research scientist, OpenAI
achievements.impact: Joined OpenAI at its founding in 2015 and worked there as a founding member and research scientist through 2017.

achievements.title: Director of AI, Tesla
achievements.impact: Led the computer vision team behind Tesla Autopilot, and briefly Optimus, overseeing data labeling, neural network training, and deployment on Tesla's custom inference chips from 2017 to 2022.

achievements.title: CS231n, Stanford University
achievements.impact: Designed and served as primary instructor for Stanford's first deep learning course, which grew from 150 students in 2015 to 750 in 2017.

achievements.title: Eureka Labs
achievements.impact: Founded an AI-native education company in 2024 after his second stint at OpenAI.
